rules.rule:
BaseShip owns shared movement, combat, shields, and module application for every ship in the project, so a change here affects player and AI alike. Enforce ALL of the following:

## Ownership boundaries
- Do NOT move physics, weapon, or shield logic into subclasses. Subclasses (PlayerShip, EnemyShip) override `_gather_commands()` and nothing else about movement or damage.
- A ship must not know whether a human or an AI is controlling it. Controller intent is expressed only through `command_heading`, `command_thrust`, and `command_fire`.

## Wrapped space
- Any distance, direction, or comparison between two positions MUST go through `SectorSpace.shortest_delta()` or `SectorSpace.wrapped_distance()`. Direct subtraction or `.distance_to()` across a sector edge is a bug.
- `global_position` must be wrapped with `SectorSpace.wrap_position()` after motion.

## Transient actors
- Projectiles, pickups, and effects must be parented via `SectorSpace.spawn_owned()`, never `get_tree().current_scene`. The Game root survives sector transitions, so parenting there leaks actors into the next sector.

## Stats and modules
- Authored stats come only from the YARD `ShipDefinition` resolved by `ship_id`. Do not hardcode numbers that belong in data.
- `_rebuild_stats()` must rebuild from the base definition before applying modules, so installs are order-independent.
- Preserve the `initializing` flag semantics: a first build fills hull and shields; a later rebuild only clamps them.

## Lifecycle
- `_die()` must stay idempotent behind `is_dead`, and must emit `died` exactly once.
- Damage must absorb into shields before hull, and only positive amounts may heal.

RunState owns mutable run state only. Authored content belongs in YARD registries, never here. Enforce ALL of the following:

## Content stays in YARD
- Do NOT add arrays, dictionaries, or hardcoded lists of ships, pilots, or modules. Content is resolved through the `MODULES` registry by stable string ID, or queried through the `category` index.
- YARD string IDs are the canonical identity. Never store or compare resource file paths.

## World simulation
- `advance_world()` is called exactly once per accepted sector transition and is the ONLY place world state advances. Do not add per-frame or timer-driven mutation.
- Completion and reward functions must stay idempotent (guard behind the existing `*_complete` flags) so repeated triggers cannot pay out twice.
- Deadlines and caps must use named constants, not bare literals.

## Signals
- Balance changes must emit both `credits_changed` and `run_state_changed`, since the HUD and mission systems listen to different ones.
- `reset_run()` must reset every persistent field together so a restart is deterministic.

## Settings
- Dev-mode preference handling must fail closed: a missing file means disabled, and unreadable or wrongly-typed data must leave it disabled rather than raising.

SectorSpace defines what wrapped space means for the entire game, so every other system depends on it being correct. Enforce ALL of the following:

## Correctness of the toroidal math
- `wrap_position()` must use `fposmod` so negative coordinates wrap into the positive sector, never a plain modulo.
- `shortest_delta()` must choose the shortest signed path independently per axis.
- Guard against a zero or negative `sector_size` before any division, modulo, or half-sector comparison.

## Ownership rules
- `effect_parent()` and `spawn_owned()` are the only sanctioned way to introduce transient actors. They must resolve the live sector, and must never fall through to `get_tree().current_scene` when a sector group exists.
- Sector membership must be dropped before a sector is freed, so a spawn cannot resolve to a dying sector.

## Presentation vs simulation
- Wrap-ghosting helpers are visual only. They must never create collision, affect gameplay position, or be counted as sensor contacts.

SectorRoot configures one authored sector scene, and its `_ready()` runs before the sector is usable. Enforce ALL of the following:

## Ordering
- Shared space must be configured first, so anything spawned afterwards uses the correct sector size.
- Persistent objective state must be restored before actors are spawned.

## Persistence
- Content the run has already resolved must not come back. If `RunState` records an objective as destroyed or expired, the corresponding actor must be freed or not spawned.
- World-simulation-driven actors (the caravan) appear only in the sector the simulation currently assigns them to, and reinforcement counts must be clamped to the authored spawn positions.

## Authoring
- All positions, sizes, and scene references belong in `@export` properties so they are set per-scene in the Inspector, not hardcoded in the script.

These are Resource schema classes. Their exported properties are the content-authoring surface. Enforce ALL of the following:

- Changes here are a content migration: adding, removing, or renaming an exported field invalidates every existing authored `.tres`. Call this out explicitly in the review.
- Keep field defaults matching the documented prototype values so a freshly created resource is usable without editing.
- Do NOT add an `id` field to `ModuleDefinition`, `ShipDefinition`, or `PilotDefinition`. The YARD registry string ID is the canonical identity, and duplicating it creates two sources of truth.
- Enum values are serialized into `.tres` files. Never reorder, insert into the middle of, or remove an enum member; append instead.
